An empty body array remains an accepted no-op, and malformed non-array body values fail validation. Ordinary `_source` responses are unchanged.

```console
cargo test invalid_search_options_fail_before_qdrant_work
```

Native support would require a defined mapping and formatting contract for every returned field, including multivalued fields and date/numeric formats. Copying arbitrary `_source` values into `fields` would falsely label source data as doc values and would miss those semantics.


---

Source: https://dstockton.github.io/qdrant-es-gateway/markdown/2026-10-19-agriculture-irrigation-inspection.md

# Which dry plots need an irrigation inspection?

A market garden's morning queue should include dry plots with recent sensor readings. An old low reading is a reason to check the sensor, not evidence to irrigate. These six synthetic snapshots deliberately include a threshold reading, stale data, a closed plot, and a missing reading age. The cutoffs are illustrative, not agronomic advice.

Use fresh `field_note_irrigation` indexes on running Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and gateway endpoints. Curl is the same client throughout: change only `ES` to select the server. Create the mapping and load the snapshots:

```sh
ES=http://localhost:19200
curl -fsS -X PUT "$ES/field_note_irrigation" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"mappings":{"properties":{"plot":{"type":"keyword"},"crop":{"type":"keyword"},"state":{"type":"keyword"},"moisture_percent":{"type":"integer"},"reading_age_minutes":{"type":"integer"}}}}'
curl -fsS -X POST "$ES/field_note_irrigation/_bulk?refresh=wait_for" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-ndjson' --data-binary @- <<'NDJSON'
{"index":{"_id":"plot-101"}}
{"plot":"North tunnel","crop":"tomato","state":"open","moisture_percent":18,"reading_age_minutes":10}
{"index":{"_id":"plot-102"}}
{"plot":"East beds","crop":"lettuce","state":"open","moisture_percent":19,"reading_age_minutes":30}
{"index":{"_id":"plot-103"}}
{"plot":"West beds","crop":"lettuce","state":"open","moisture_percent":20,"reading_age_minutes":5}
{"index":{"_id":"plot-104"}}
{"plot":"South tunnel","crop":"tomato","state":"open","moisture_percent":12,"reading_age_minutes":31}
{"index":{"_id":"plot-105"}}
{"plot":"Trial beds","crop":"lettuce","state":"closed","moisture_percent":15,"reading_age_minutes":8}
{"index":{"_id":"plot-106"}}
{"plot":"Herb beds","crop":"basil","state":"open","moisture_percent":16}
NDJSON
sleep 5
```

The same five-second pause follows each write phase on all three servers; this is a settling allowance, not a refresh guarantee. Reading ages are fixed snapshots for a deterministic example; a real ingestion process must refresh them.

Find open plots below 20% moisture with a reading no more than 30 minutes old:

```sh
curl -fsS -X POST "$ES/field_note_irrigation/_search" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"size":10,"query":{"bool":{"filter":[{"term":{"state":"open"}},{"range":{"moisture_percent":{"lt":20}}},{"range":{"reading_age_minutes":{"lte":30}}}]}}}'
```

Expect exactly `plot-101` and `plot-102`, complete sources, and total `2`; order does not matter. The 20% boundary, 31-minute reading, closed plot, and missing age must all be excluded. Count crops within that same queue:

```sh
curl -fsS -X POST "$ES/field_note_irrigation/_search" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"size":0,"query":{"bool":{"filter":[{"term":{"state":"open"}},{"range":{"moisture_percent":{"lt":20}}},{"range":{"reading_age_minutes":{"lte":30}}}]}},"aggs":{"crops":{"terms":{"field":"crop","size":10}}}}'
```

Expect `tomato: 1` and `lettuce: 1`, with no hits. These are plot counts, not water requirements. After inspecting the North tunnel, remove it from the queue without overwriting its sensor snapshot:

```sh
curl -fsS -X POST "$ES/field_note_irrigation/_update/plot-101?refresh=wait_for" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"doc":{"state":"inspected"}}'
sleep 5
curl -fsS -X GET "$ES/field_note_irrigation/_doc/plot-101"
```

The update returns `updated`. The read retains the plot, crop, 18% moisture, and 10-minute reading age, with `state: "inspected"`. Repeat both search requests: only `plot-102` remains, total `1`, and the only bucket is `lettuce: 1`.

The [fixture](https://github.com/dstockton/qdrant-es-gateway/blob/main/validation/fixtures/agriculture.json), [replay](https://github.com/dstockton/qdrant-es-gateway/blob/main/validation/agriculture.py), and [recorded evidence](https://github.com/dstockton/qdrant-es-gateway/blob/main/validation/evidence/agriculture-2026-10-19.json) verify statuses, bulk IDs/results, every source, exact search IDs/totals, crop counts, and inspection exclusion. The run passed 105/105 checks on native Elasticsearch 8.15.0, native OpenSearch 3.9.0, and gateway 0.2.0 with Qdrant 1.15.5, using identical requests and embedded sources with synchronous writes. No OpenSearch-specific behavior or assertion difference was observed. The article's curl requests were also executed on all three endpoints. No gateway change or performance claim is involved.

Boundary: [atomic concurrent updates](https://dstockton.github.io/qdrant-es-gateway/compatibility/) are unsupported; this queue does not control irrigation equipment.

Remove the example index:

```sh
curl -fsS -X DELETE "$ES/field_note_irrigation"
```

Source: https://dstockton.github.io/qdrant-es-gateway/markdown/2026-10-18-query-profiles-cannot-be-empty.md

# Query profiles cannot be empty

The gateway accepted `profile: true` in a search body but ignored it. That turns a diagnostic request into an ordinary search while still returning HTTP 200. It is especially misleading here because the gateway executes against Qdrant, not Lucene: a native-looking query and collector timing tree cannot be inferred from the returned hits.

A focused probe used the same mapped fields, three-document corpus, and match query against separate Elasticsearch 8.15.0 and OpenSearch 3.9.0 containers. Both returned a top-level `profile` object with one shard, a `TermQuery` timing breakdown, and collector data. The observed collectors differed: Elasticsearch reported `QueryPhaseCollector`, while OpenSearch reported `TopScoreDocCollector`. For this small compact response, enabling profiling increased the body from 419 to 2,124 bytes in Elasticsearch and from 420 to 1,758 bytes in OpenSearch. Those byte counts illustrate response shaping only; they are not a latency, CPU, allocation, or throughput benchmark.

The sanitized [request and response evidence](https://github.com/dstockton/qdrant-es-gateway/blob/main/validation/evidence/elasticsearch-8.15-opensearch-3.9-search-profile-2026-10-18.json) records the images, corpus, selected response fields, reproduction sequence, and limitations. The [Elasticsearch search profiling documentation](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/search-profile.html) and [OpenSearch Profile API documentation](https://docs.opensearch.org/latest/api-reference/search-apis/profile/) independently describe their profiling responses and overhead cautions.

The gateway now rejects `profile: true` before index lookup or Qdrant access, including in each `_msearch` subrequest. Explicit `profile: false` remains accepted, and non-boolean JSON values fail validation instead of being ignored. The focused regression proves the rejected requests perform no upstream work:

```console
cargo test invalid_search_options_fail_before_qdrant_work
```

Existing searches that omit `profile` or set it to `false` are unchanged. Implementing gateway-native profiling later would require an explicitly different schema that reports gateway and Qdrant phases honestly rather than borrowing Lucene component names.

Source: https://dstockton.github.io/qdrant-es-gateway/markdown/2026-10-18-production-stack-refresh.md

# Refreshing the production stack without opening old volumes

The development and benchmark stack now uses Rust 1.99.1, Qdrant 1.19.2, Valkey 9.1.2, HAProxy 3.4.7, Python 3.15.0, and Elasticsearch 9.5.5. The Rust client layer also moves to reqwest 0.13 and redis-rs 1.7. This is a maintenance update: the existing client and demo request shapes are unchanged.

Fresh ephemeral containers provide the evidence for this update. Elasticsearch reported version **9.5.5** and a green single-node cluster; Qdrant reported **1.19.2** and passed the gateway's live create, bulk, search, and delete smoke path; all seven shared-catalog tests passed against Valkey **9.1.2**. The gateway image built from an empty cache, the benchmark image built, all three Compose files parsed, 92 isolated Rust tests and one live integration test passed, and formatting, Clippy, and `cargo audit` were clean. A refreshed Trivy database found no fixed HIGH or CRITICAL vulnerabilities in the gateway image. The [sanitized evidence](https://github.com/dstockton/qdrant-es-gateway/blob/main/validation/evidence/production-stack-refresh-2026-10-18.json) records the versions, results, and limitations.

The important operational result is a boundary, not a shortcut. Elasticsearch 9.5.5 reports minimum wire compatibility with 8.19.0, so an 8.15 benchmark volume must first follow Elastic's [upgrade preparation](https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/upgrade/prepare-to-upgrade) through the latest 8.19 patch. Qdrant documents consecutive minor upgrades, so a 1.15 volume must be backed up and opened by the latest 1.15, 1.16, 1.17, and 1.18 patches before 1.19.2; the [migration guide](https://dstockton.github.io/qdrant-es-gateway/migration/) records that sequence. No existing volume was opened during validation.

This run did **not** change or exercise OpenSearch. The Elasticsearch 9.5.5 result is an Elasticsearch-specific benchmark-environment check, not evidence that OpenSearch behaves the same way. It is also not a compatibility replay or throughput benchmark. Reproduce the bounded startup checks on fresh storage with:

```sh
docker run --rm -d --name qeg-es-check \
  -p 127.0.0.1:19200:9200 \
  -e discovery.type=single-node -e xpack.security.enabled=false \
  docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch/elasticsearch:9.5.5
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19200/
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19200/_cluster/health

docker run --rm -d --name qeg-qdrant-check \
  -p 127.0.0.1:16333:6333 qdrant/qdrant:v1.19.2
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:16333/
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:16333/readyz
```

Stop those temporary containers after the check; do not attach old data volumes to these commands.

Source: https://dstockton.github.io/qdrant-es-gateway/markdown/2026-10-17-score-explanations-must-explain-the-score.md

# Score explanations must explain the score

The gateway accepted `explain: true` in a search body but ignored it. That is not merely missing decoration: clients use each hit's `_explanation` tree to debug ranking, and the gateway's score comes from Qdrant rather than Lucene. Fabricating a Lucene-shaped explanation or silently omitting it would both misdescribe how the result was ranked.

A focused probe used the same mapped text field, one-document corpus, and match query against separate Elasticsearch 8.15.0 and OpenSearch 3.9.0 containers. Both added `_shard`, `_node`, and a nested `_explanation` to the matching hit. The engines did not produce identical output: Elasticsearch reported score `0.2876821` and included an explicit boost component, while OpenSearch reported `0.13076457` without that component in this version pair. The sanitized [request and response evidence](https://github.com/dstockton/qdrant-es-gateway/blob/main/validation/evidence/elasticsearch-8.15-opensearch-3.9-search-explain-2026-10-17.json) records the images, request, selected response fields, reproduction sequence, and limitations. The [Elasticsearch Search API](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/search-search.html) and [OpenSearch Search API](https://docs.opensearch.org/latest/api-reference/search-apis/search/) independently document the per-hit explanation contract.

The gateway now rejects `explain: true` before index lookup or Qdrant access, including in each `_msearch` subrequest. Explicit `explain: false` remains accepted, and non-boolean values fail validation instead of being ignored. The focused regression proves the rejected requests perform no upstream work:

```console
cargo test invalid_search_options_fail_before_qdrant_work
```

This is request/response compatibility evidence, not a relevance or performance benchmark. The score difference should not be generalized to all Elasticsearch and OpenSearch versions, mappings, or queries. Existing searches that omit `explain` or set it to `false` are unchanged.

Source: https://dstockton.github.io/qdrant-es-gateway/markdown/2026-10-17-highlight-snippets-cannot-vanish.md

# Highlight snippets cannot vanish

The gateway accepted a search `highlight` object but ignored it. That changes the response contract: clients commonly request snippets to show where a result matched, and a successful response without those snippets can render an empty preview or force an unsafe fallback to the complete source text.

A focused probe used the same one-document corpus and request against separate Elasticsearch 8.15.0 and OpenSearch 3.9.0 containers. Both returned HTTP 200 and added `{"title":["wireless <em>headphones</em> for travel"]}` under the matching hit's `highlight` field. This independently confirms the contract for both targets; it does not assume OpenSearch behavior from Elasticsearch. The sanitized [request and response evidence](https://github.com/dstockton/qdrant-es-gateway/blob/main/validation/evidence/elasticsearch-8.15-opensearch-3.9-highlight-2026-10-17.json) records the images, versions, fixture, request, result, reproduction sequence, and limitations. The [Elasticsearch](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/highlighting) and [OpenSearch](https://docs.opensearch.org/latest/search-plugins/searching-data/highlight/) references likewise describe the per-hit response field.

The gateway now rejects `highlight` before index lookup or Qdrant access. Implementing it honestly would require analyzer-aware match offsets, fragment boundaries and scoring, multi-field rules, source/stored-field behavior, and engine-specific option validation. Returning ordinary hits while dropping the request is not a safe approximation. The focused regression proves both `_search` and each `_msearch` subrequest inherit the same fail-closed path without sending an upstream request:

```console
cargo test invalid_search_options_fail_before_qdrant_work
```

This is request-level compatibility evidence, not a performance result. It covers one ordinary text field with the default highlighter; it does not claim identical Elasticsearch and OpenSearch behavior for other highlighters, analyzers, fragments, or versions. Existing searches without `highlight` are unchanged.
